1. (Currently Amended): A method of treating a brain, comprising: inserting an elongated device into the brain to create a path; radially expanding the device to create a working channel along the path; and introducing a medical element into the working channel to perform a medical procedure on the brain, wherein the elongated device is inserted through an opening created in a cranium.

2. (Currently Amended): The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is a medical instrument.

4. (Currently Amended): The method of claim 1, further comprising inserting the elongated device in a manner not confined to between tissue layers within the brain. 

5. (Currently Amended): The method of claim 1, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue structures within the brain.

7. (Currently Amended): A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the device against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially reinforcing the device against the tissue; and introducing a medical element through the device to perform a medical procedure on the tissue, wherein the method does not necessarily require the device to radially displace all tissue layers along the path.

8. (Currently Amended): The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is a medical instrument.

10. (Currently Amended): The method of claim 7, further comprising inserting the elongated device randomly among or within tissue structures. 

13. (Currently Amended): A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device, having a first radially expandable body, surrounded by a stent, which is surrounded by a second radially expandable body, into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the second expandable body against the tissue to radially displace the tissue; radially expanding the first expandable body to radially expand the stent to enhance the support provided to the second expandable body; radially contracting and safely removing the first expandable body to create a working channel through the stent; introducing a medical element through the channel to perform a medical procedure on the tissue; and radially contracting the second expandable body and safely removing the device from the tissue. 

14. (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is a medical instrument.
